title: laya-phase-4.2-prediction-result
description: Canonical, adapter-agnostic prediction record. Any evaluated system (a deterministic prefilter, Claude, Laya, JEV, or a future baseline) reports one result per corpus row in exactly this shape, so scoring code never branches on which adapter produced it. Adapters are NOT implemented in this slice; this schema exists so later slices have a fixed target. No adapter-specific fields are permitted here -- adapter-specific detail belongs only in raw_response.

candidate_id.description: The corpus row this prediction is for. Result-bookkeeping metadata only -- never present in the rendered model input itself.

run_id.description: Identifies one evaluation run (a batch of predictions produced together), so repeated runs of the same corpus can be told apart.

model_identifier.description: Free-text identifier of the system that produced the prediction, e.g. 'deterministic_prefilter_v1', 'claude-sonnet-5', 'laya_v0'. Not an enum -- new systems must not require a schema change.

predicted_value.description: The system's chosen output, restricted to the allowed_output_values of the matching prompt contract. Null when the system produced no usable answer (see valid_prediction/error).

valid_prediction.description: True only if predicted_value is one of the prompt contract's allowed_output_values. False for a malformed, empty, or off-contract response -- scoring code must never coerce an invalid value into a guess.

confidence.description: Optional self-reported confidence in [0,1]. Null when the system does not provide one -- never fabricated.

probability_distribution.description: Optional map of allowed_output_value -> probability, for systems that expose one (e.g. a deterministic rule or a calibrated classifier). Null when unavailable.

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time to produce this one prediction. Null when not measured (e.g. a deterministic rule with negligible, unmeasured cost).

input_tokens.description: Null for adapters with no token concept (e.g. a deterministic rule).

error.description: Non-null describes what went wrong (timeout, refusal, malformed output, leakage-preflight failure, etc.); null means the call completed without error, independent of whether the prediction was valid.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC time the prediction was produced.

corpus_content_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the exact corpus file this prediction was scored against (see the corpus loader), so a result can never be silently compared against a corpus revision it wasn't produced from.

raw_response.description: Opaque, adapter-specific debugging payload (e.g. the full model response). Never read by scoring code; present only for post-hoc inspection.
